```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "#>")
library(metacheck)
```

## What it checks

The `ref_retraction` module cross-references the paper's **cited references** against the [Retraction Watch](https://retractionwatch.com/) database. Citing a retracted article — usually unknowingly — is a common and avoidable problem. The module flags any cited reference that appears in the Retraction Watch database so you can check whether the citation is still appropriate. The database records retractions, but also corrections and expressions of concern; the report shows which applies to each flagged reference.

::: callout-note
This module runs **offline**: it matches references by DOI against a copy of the Retraction Watch database that ships with Metacheck, so the code below needs no internet connection. Only updating that copy with `rw_update()` (see [Updating the database](#updating-the-database)) downloads data.
:::

## Running the module

::: {.callout-note}
## Without R
This module also runs on [Metacheck's website](https://metacheckserve.metacheck.src.surf-hosted.nl/): upload a paper under *Run Metacheck on a Paper*, and tick it under *Checks* (it is not one of the default checks). The [Docker installation](get-started.qmd#docker-installation) offers the same website on your own computer. The website runs the module with its default settings; to change them, run it in R as below.
:::

`demopaper()` cites a reference that is in the Retraction Watch database.

```{r}
paper <- demopaper()
mo <- module_run(paper, "ref_retraction")
mo$traffic_light
mo$summary_text
```

The `table` lists each cited reference found in the database:

```{r}
mo$table[, c("doi", "text")] |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Running on many papers

```{r}
#| eval: false
mo <- module_run(psychsci[1:10], "ref_retraction")
mo$summary_table
```

## Interpreting the result

A flagged reference is not automatically a mistake — retractions happen for many reasons, and a retracted paper is sometimes cited deliberately (for example, to discuss the retraction itself). The module's job is to make sure you are *aware*, so you can decide. Follow up each flagged DOI before acting.

## Options

`ref_retraction` takes only the `paper` argument.

## Updating the database

The module matches references against a data frame that ships with Metacheck, which the function `retractionwatch()` (or its short form `rw()`) returns. New retractions are recorded constantly, so the bundled copy gradually goes out of date. Two functions help you manage it:

```{r}
#| eval: false
rw_date()     # the date the bundled database was last updated
rw_update()   # download the newest version from Retraction Watch
```

`rw_update()` downloads the latest Retraction Watch data (>50 MB), summarises it into a compact form (~0.5 MB), deletes the large original, and caches the result so subsequent checks use the fresh data. Run it occasionally — or before an important check — to make sure you are not missing recent retractions.

## Notes

This is the same kind of check that reference managers such as [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/blog/retracted-item-notifications/) perform, brought into the Metacheck workflow so it can run alongside the other reference checks.
